newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, May 20 - There were no suprises in PORLA's latest release. The figures on CPO production, palm oil stocks and total offtake were all close to our estimates. Production rose 7.2 percent or 49,500 tonnes to 733,200 tonnes. Peninsular Malaysia production was up by a modest 5.2 percent or well below the 13.5 percent posted by East Malaysia. For the first four months of this year, production expanded 10.9 percent or 245,500 tonnes to 2.50 million tonnes. East Malaysia accounted for 58 percent of the increase when its output grew strongly by 27.6 percent or 142,600 tonnes.

Production in Peninsular Malaysia rose at a modest rate of around 6 percent and looked likely to shrink to a low single-digit growth rate in May-June and stagnant in the last 6 months of the year. End April stocks of palm oil rose 7,500 tonnes to 697,700 tonnes or just a shade higher than our estimate of 695,000 tonnes. Stocks of CPO alone shrank 11,800 tonnes to 350,400 tonnes. Not surprisingly, stocks in Peninsular Malaysia fell 17,600 tonnes to 230,500 tonnes and well below the year-ago level of 380,100 tonnes.

We expect only minor relief in the tight CPO supply situation in Peninsular Malaysia in May-June as CPO arrivals from East Malaysia are projected to improve by not more than 10,000 tonnes a month during this period. This is based on our estimate of modest month-on-month increases in CPO output. For this month, our tentative estimate shows a rise in production of just over 3 percent or around 25,000 tonnes to 758,000 tonnes. Total palm oil offtake or dissappearance (inclusive of refining losses) remained good at 725,700 tonnes in April as against 717,000 tonnes in the preceding month.

However, PORLA's palm oil exports figures at 570,100 tonnes (preliminary) in April versus 579,600 tonnes in March appeared to have spooked some players in the market. The implied 'domestic' dissappearance figure (inclusive of refining losses) of 155,600 tonnes in April and 137,300 tonnes in March are abnormally high. We belief the export figures are incomplete or under-reported. For the 12 months to December 1996, PORLA's final palm oil exports of 7,211,900 tonnes fell short of the department of statistics' figures of 7,310,300 tonnes by 98,400 tonnes or an average of 8,200 tonnes a month.

Twice last year, the monthly shortfall exceeded 50,000 tonnes. PORLA's latest figures should not be cited as a factor contributing to the drop in prices last week. July CPO futures fell 24 ringgit on May 15-16 bringing the week's losses to 34 ringgit. The losses were attributed to concern that palm oil exports this month could drop some 50,000 tonnes. New export sales were also sluggish.

A third factor contributing to the weakness in palm oil prices was the strength of the ringgit which settled at 2.4890 a dollar last Friday, up 185 points from a week earlier and after an intra-week low of 2.525 on May 14 caused by spillover weakness from the Thai baht.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
